title: Adventurer’s Guild
paragraphs: I was just about to repeat what Father had said last time.
“No need to say it.”
“Yeah.”
“I’ve heard Motoyasu-kun’s story a few times now. He probably said it was a gal game world.”
Oh? He saw right through me completely. And he was right. As expected of Father.
“Ren’s world probably had incidents where dying in a game meant dying in real life, right?”

“You’ve been reading too many novels. There were some fantasies like that back when VR first emerged in my world, but at most… there was an incident where developers went rogue, using accelerated in-game time perception to make players believe that dying in the game meant actual death.”
“That actually happened?”

“Apparently, a long time ago. During an open test, players who logged in within the first hour were tricked into thinking that was the case. Of course, no one actually died, and it was dismissed as an over-the-top event by the developers.”
“I bet that game got shut down.”
“Some people were arrested. But in my world, it’s widely believed that ‘dying in a game = dying in real life’ is virtually impossible.”
Wow, hearing about Ren’s world is pretty refreshing. It sounds like a lot of incidents happened there. What about mine?
…Come to think of it, I don’t recall hearing about any major incidents. Honestly, I was more focused on chasing pigs than following public opinion, so I don’t know much.
“You’d think there would’ve been cases of brain hacking, though. In VR-related light novels from my world, ‘brainwashing’ comes up pretty frequently.”
“Science hasn’t advanced that far. Though, given time, maybe it could have happened.”
Ren muttered something under his breath.
“After all… it was a world where sensation was almost nonexistent. Your consciousness could enter the internet, but… I haven’t studied the difference enough to fully understand it yet.”
“So it was more like just looking at a game screen?”
“Body movements were replicated, but there was no pain or touch. At most, the equipment simulated vibrations, like damage effects.”
“I see.”
Ren, who doesn’t usually talk much, was explaining a lot to Father.
“But apparently, some people mistook it for reality, so they had to lower the resolution.”
“Huh… so there were side effects like that, too.”
“Just like absolute pitch, some people had a natural ability to perceive immersion even at lower resolutions. Those people… were definitely tough opponents in games.”
At that moment, Father seemed to realize something but changed the subject by looking over at Itsuki. Does Itsuki have something to do with Ren’s story?
“I bet there were people with special abilities like that in Itsuki’s world, too.”
“There were. They were called ‘Net Divers’—people who could submerge their consciousness into the digital world. To them, the internet might have been a kind of VR.”
“See? Itsuki’s world is always more interesting.”
“Don’t push the conversation in that direction! And Ren-san, don’t just nod along! Please, let’s keep enjoying Ren-san’s story!”

“Hmm… but even if we talk about VR games, we’re already in another world. And from what I hear, everyday life there was just slightly futuristic—cars didn’t even fly—so it doesn’t sound all that different.”
“A world where people can fly with special abilities is more fun. At least, for now.”
“Ugh!”
Itsuki looked frustrated, but he didn’t seem to completely dislike it. After all, he enjoys having people listen to him.
“The Hero-donos truly come from unusual worlds. I enjoy hearing about any of them,” Éclair murmured, making Father and the others look slightly embarrassed.

“A world without levels… I wonder what that would be like? I can’t grasp the difference between supernatural abilities and magic, and I don’t know what this ‘VR’ is, but it sounds like something from a dream. In that sense, the worlds where Iwatani-dono and Kitamura-dono lived seem more like otherworlds to me.”

“That’s an interesting perspective. But based on what Ren, Itsuki, and Motoyasu have said, my world is probably closest to a version of this one where Faubrey’s technology has spread, but without magic.”
“I see.”
We continued chatting like that for a while. After some time, Éclair spoke up.
“Hmm… Well then, shall we wrap up our break and resume training?”
“Food will be ready soon, so let’s eat first. Either way, it seems like our only option is to keep getting stronger.”
“Going back to the topic… what exactly should I do?”
“Basically, as an archer, you’re already complete, right? So aside from that, your best bet is probably to focus on evasion techniques… like a ninja or something.”
“That just means I’ll be relying on level-based brute force in the end, doesn’t it…? Haah.”
Itsuki sighed deeply. Well, gaining strength outside of leveling up is tough. Even Father had to train for days.
“By the way, in your original world, you could handle firearms as well. You copied them in Faubrey, right?”
“Huh? It wasn’t just bows!? What kind of weapon variety do I even have!?”
“If we go by modern standards… You can use guns, so you’re like a ranger unit or something? Gun kata is pretty cool, too.”
“At this rate, I really won’t have anything to do except train my body and dodge…”
“Better than doing nothing, don’t you think?”
At my words, Father, Ren, and Éclair all nodded.
“I envy Ren. Compared to him, my role is just to dodge… even more restricted than Naofumi’s.”
“I think you’d at least be allowed to parry, so you can still participate.”
Hearing that, Itsuki’s expression brightened slightly as he looked at Father. Seems like he really dislikes being left out.
“That said… we can’t deny that we have people with little experience swinging around weapons.”
“That can’t be helped. Even if we’re called Heroes, we’re just ordinary people from a peaceful Japan.”
“We should just follow in the footsteps of our past selves and work on improving our skills outside of level grinding. Right, Motoyasu-kun?”
“Indeed.”
“If you can get to the point where you can dodge attacks from all three of the Filolials at once, then you won’t have to be afraid anymore.”
“Naofumi-san, you just said something crazy like it was nothing.”
“Can we even do that? We can barely dodge Éclair’s attacks as it is.”
“Alright then, Yuki-chan and the others! It’s time for today’s play session!”
“We’re doing this right now!?”
I called over Yuki-chan and the others, who had already finished eating, and we continued the game we’ve been playing for the past few days. It was a game Father had come up with—trying to catch me.
“Today, we will definitely catch you, Motoyasu-sama!”
“Kou will do her best!”
“Sakura’s getting bored—I wanna play with Naofumi instead!”
Despite their complaints, Yuki-chan’s sharp kicks, Kou’s surprise attacks, and Sakura-chan’s reckless charges kept coming, but I skillfully dodged them all.
“Like that…”
“Seems possible after all.”
“Yeah. Let’s do our best to improve our skills.”
“But first, dinner.”
And so, another night passed.
“So this is the Adventurers’ Guild… Every time I see it; it just reminds me of a government office. Or maybe a job placement center?”
“Please don’t say such sad things. Now I can’t help but see the adventurers as unemployed people.”

While stopping by a town, Father and the others visited the Adventurers’ Guild to observe the state of the world. Since this place was a key source of information, Éclair and I often came here. Yuki-chan and the others were curiously looking around—it was quite adorable.
“Is this the quest counter?”
Father’s eyes turned to the documents posted on the board. None of them seemed to be particularly well-paying requests. Mostly cheap quests.
“Most of them seem to be simple chores around the area. Adventurers pick out jobs they like and take them on.”
Éclair pointed to one of the requests.
“This one is a joint request from the Merchants’ Guild. It’s for gathering medicinal herbs.”
“A classic herb-gathering quest. Barely pocket change, right?”
“It seems the herbs grow in a dangerous area. The reward is actually a bit better than usual.”
“What about people who can’t read?”
“For those individuals, there are staff members who are fluent in various languages. They also handle high-value requests.”
“Éclair, have you ever taken on one of these?”
“No, I haven’t. As a knight, I only know about them in a general sense—it’s all second-hand knowledge.”
Father and the others continued to browse the area with interest.
“Oh? They have wanted posters here, like bounties. And they even include full-body images.”
“That’s actually an impressive technology.”
Next to the quest counter, Father pointed at an image crystal displaying footage of criminals. Like a hologram, it showed everything—from their faces to their full body height.
